title: Kali Steps on Shiva
hookLine: a goddess dancing after battle who can't stop, and a god who lies down in her path
carry: shiva and shakti: stillness and power, never apart
tomorrow: a garland in the dirt, and the day lakshmi left

cards: The battle is over, the demons gone, and Kali is still dancing. In the story people tell, she can't come down from it. Her feet pound the ground until it cracks.
The worlds shake. The gods, cheering a moment ago, look at one another in alarm. Who will stop her?

Nobody wants to walk up to Kali mid-dance and tap her on the shoulder. Then one of them has an idea, and it isn't a fight. It's an odd move, and it's the scene behind images of Kali standing on someone.

teach.h: SHIVA LIES DOWN IN HER PATH.
teach.b: The gods go to Shiva. He doesn't pick up a weapon or argue with her. He walks onto the battlefield and lies down among the fallen, right in her path.

teach.h: SHE STEPS ON HIM, AND SEES HIM.
teach.b: Kali, dancing blind, steps on him, looks down, and sees who it is: her own husband, under her foot.
In one Bengali telling, that's when her tongue comes out, the way someone bites their tongue in shock: oh no, what have I done. And the dance stops. This story isn't in the Devi Mahatmya.
It grew up around Kali afterward, and it's told more than one way. Some tellings say Shiva lay down to calm her; some, so she'd recognize him. The point isn't that he beat her.
Nobody beats Kali. He stopped her by being still, and by being someone she loves.

teach.h: SHIVA AND SHAKTI: STILL AND MOVING.
teach.b: Many teachers read a big Hindu teaching in the picture: Shiva and Shakti.

teach.h: STOPPED BY STILLNESS, AND BY LOVE.
teach.b: Shiva lying there, motionless and pale, is stillness, pure awareness. Kali, dark and moving, is Shakti, power, everything that happens. The two are never really apart.

A well-known hymn, the Saundarya Lahari, opens by saying Shiva can create only when joined with Shakti; without her he can't even stir. The dance needs the ground, and the ground on its own doesn't dance.

Others simply love it as a family story: a wife so caught up she didn't see her husband, and the look on her face when she did. Either way, the character comes through. Kali's fierceness is real, and it stops for love.

how: In Bengal and elsewhere, images of Kali standing on Shiva, her tongue out, are found in temples and homes, and devotees read the scene both as a family story and as a picture of stillness and power together.

o: the great Goddess, whose fierce form is Kali
a dance that shakes the worlds after battle
the still god who lies down in Kali's path

p: shock at whom she stepped on

s: the story of Kali stepping on Shiva comes from the Devi Mahatmya
it's one of the stories that grew up around Kali afterward, and it's told more than one way.
in the story, Shiva stops Kali by fighting her
he doesn't fight; he lies down in her path, and she stops when she sees who it is.

Shiva lying still, Kali dark and moving: the dance needs the ground, and the two are never apart.

games.q: you're one of the gods. the demons are gone, but Kali is still dancing, and the worlds are cracking. what works?
o: Shiva lies down, still, in her path
wait for her to get tired
games.why: in the story, Shiva lies down among the fallen. Kali steps on him, sees her husband, and the dance stops.

practice: Sit, or lie down if you can, and let the body be completely still, the way Shiva was, while the breath, the heartbeat, racing thoughts and sounds outside keep moving.

Don't stop any of it; be the still ground it moves over, Shiva under Shakti's dance, and if one thought keeps dancing, let it dance. If you pray, rest in the Goddess's presence; if you don't, rest in the stillness.

wordCard.voice: Durga. The name over this stretch of five characters, and today, the goddess whose fierce form, as Kali, dances until stillness stops her. Today's word.

carryVoice: Your line: shiva and shakti, stillness and power, never apart. Tomorrow, Lakshmi, and the day she left. Rest well.
